- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >10%), model often overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- If forecast mean is significantly above true mean (e.g., >15% over 30d), apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment volatility.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drop.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 20% drop from peak), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast.
